description: Shared contract corpus for the ingredient expression language: expressions the platform calculation engine accepts or refuses. Consumed by whereClauseCorpus.spec.ts in this package and mirrored into the Albert Python SDK (albert-python tests/unit/utils/calculation_expression_corpus.json), whose client-side validator asserts the same verdicts. When the language changes (new functions, WHERE at ingredient basis, multi-select Function), update this file and the SDK mirror together.

fields.expression: The raw, display-name expression as a user writes it.
fields.platform: accepted | rejected: the platform's end verdict on the expression.
fields.stage: For rejected entries: normalize = refused while rewriting/parsing the expression; evaluate = normalization succeeds but the expression cannot compile. Client-side pre-save checks reject both stages.
fields.rule: Stable identifier of the rule that rejects the expression, for rejected entries.

entries.note: Whitespace around the equals sign is optional.
OR includes several values of the same key.

entries.expression: sum(wt% WHERE Function = "Core" OR Function = "Shell" OR Function = "Binder")

entries.note: A text property attribute in brackets can filter instead of Function; single quotes are accepted.
An attribute ID can key the filter.
Share-of-sum (PHR): a filtered sum as a shared denominator.
The WHERE filter applies after a compound inner expression.
Weighted harmonic mean over all ingredients.
An ingredient carries one value per filter key, so AND would match nothing; use OR.
Only equality against a quoted value is supported.
Known limitation: an OR word inside a quoted value splits the clause. Write OR between conditions instead.
All OR branches of one WHERE filter must use the same key.

entries.expression: sum(wt% WHERE Function = "Core" OR Function = "Shell" AND Function = "Binder")

entries.note: Normalization succeeds but nothing is left to sum, so compilation fails.
A WHERE keyword without a condition fails at compilation.
